newsitem.title: HUNGARY: HUNGARY WATCHDOG EXTENDS CURBS ON VEKTOR BROKER.
newsitem.headline: HUNGARY WATCHDOG EXTENDS CURBS ON VEKTOR BROKER.

text.p: Hungary's bourse watchdog has extended until January 31 the restrictions it imposed on Vektor Broker Rt last October.

"The company's accounting has not been separated from that of Vektor Penzugyi Befektetesi Tanacsado Rt (Vektor PBT) as the documents of the two companies are bound up with each other," the State Securiites and Bourse supervision (AETF) said in the official bourse gazette Magyar Tokepiac.

Financial consulting company Vektor PBT represented local authorities in negotiations with privatisation agency APV Rt over asset transfers the municipalities were due in exchange for land on which privatised state companies were based.

APV's negotiator, Marta Tocsik, triggered a scandal resulting in the sacking of privatisation minister Tamas Suchman and the entire APV board when it became public that she had received a 804 million forints success fee.
A parliamentary committee is looking into the affair while Hungary's Chief Prosecutor has initiated criminal proceedings.
Press reports said that the 16 billion forints Vektor PBT negotiated for municipalities, had appeared on Vektor Broker's accounts.
Although this transfer was not illegal in itself, the unclear boundaries between Vektor Broker and Vektor PBT raised some doubts regarding investors' secirity, AETF said.
"The supervision has established that (Vektor Broker's) activity...could jeopardise the interests of investors," the authority said.
The decision, published on Friday, was brought by AETF on the last day of independent existence before being merged with the State Banking Supervision on January 1.
